An elderly female patient, aged 75, is brought to the emergency department due to progressive
dyspnea over the past week. After being diagnosed with pneumonia, she is hospitalized and treated
with daily intravenous levofloxacin 750 mg for two weeks. On day 15 of her hospital stay, she
experiences three episodes of diarrhea. The following day, her laboratory results show a white blood
cell count of 21,000/mm3, and she develops abdominal pain. Her vital signs show a pulse of 117/min,
respiratory rate of 17/min, and blood pressure of 123/57 mm Hg. During physical examination, she
appears confused and exhibits diffuse abdominal tenderness without guarding, rebound tenderness, or
rigidity. What is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Abdominal
computed tomography scan (B) Intravenous fidaxomicin (C) Stool cultures and intravenous fluids (D)
Oral metronidazole (E) Fecal microbiota transplantation (F) Intravenous vancomycin (G) Exploratory
laparotomy (H) Serial abdominal examinations (I) Diagnostic colonoscopy (J) Empiric broad-spectrum
antibiotics
 A. Fecal microbiota transplantation
B. Abdominal computed tomography scan
C. Exploratory laparotomy
D. Serial abdominal examinations
E. Intravenous vancomycin
F. Stool cultures and intravenous fluids
G. Intravenous fidaxomicin
H. Oral metronidazole
I. Diagnostic colonoscopy
J. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics
